grammar.title: Was / were + there was / there were
grammar.explanation_pt:
O passado do verbo to be tem só duas formas:
- **was** → I, he, she, it
- **were** → you, we, they

**Negativa:** wasn't / weren't · **Pergunta:** Was he...? / Were they...?

**There was / there were** = "tinha / havia" (no passado):
- There **was** a problem. (singular)
- There **were** many people. (plural)

**Expressões de passado:**
- **yesterday** (ontem), **yesterday morning**
- **last** + night/week/month/year/Friday (sem the!)
- tempo + **ago**: two hours ago, five years ago (ago vem **depois**)

rows: Yes, I was. / No, I wasn't.
Yes, she was. / No, she wasn't.
Yes, they were. / No, they weren't.

examples.en: Where were you yesterday? I was at the dentist.
examples.pt: Onde você estava ontem? Estava no dentista.

examples.en: The concert was amazing, but there were too many people.
examples.pt: O show foi incrível, mas tinha gente demais.

examples.en: I wasn't at the meeting. Was it important?
examples.pt: Eu não estava na reunião. Foi importante?

grammar.tip_pt: Repare que **was/were** traduzem **era, estava, foi** ao mesmo tempo. "It was great" = Foi ótimo. "I was tired" = Eu estava cansado. "He was a teacher" = Ele era professor.

common_mistakes.wrong: Had many people at the party.
common_mistakes.right: There were many people at the party.

common_mistakes.wrong: I was there ago two years.
common_mistakes.right: I was there two years ago.
common_mistakes.why_pt: Ago vem depois do período de tempo.

pronunciation.tip_pt: Na frase, **was** e **were** são fracos: "I wəz tired" ("ái uâz"), "We wər late" ("uí uâr"). Mas na resposta curta e na negativa são fortes: "Yes, I **WAS**." / "I **WASN'T**."

grammar.title: Simple past completo
grammar.explanation_pt:
**Afirmativa:** verbo no passado — igual para todas as pessoas.
- Regulares: **-ed** (worked, played, studied, stopped)
- Irregulares: forma própria (went, got, bought) — veja a tabela de verbos no fim do módulo e **memorize em chunks** ("I got home", "I bought a...").

**Negativa:** **didn't** + verbo **base**
- I **didn't go**. She **didn't buy** it. (nunca "didn't went")

**Pergunta:** **Did** + sujeito + verbo **base**?
- **Did** you **see** the game? — Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
- **What did** you **do**? / **Where did** she **go**? / **When did** they **arrive**?

**Ortografia dos regulares:** study → stud**ied** (consoante + y) · stop → sto**pp**ed (CVC) · like → lik**ed** (termina em e: só +d).

grammar.tip_pt: Com **was/were** não se usa did: "**Were** you tired?" (e não "Did you be tired?"). Did é para todos os outros verbos.

common_mistakes.why_pt: Depois de didn't, o verbo volta à forma base.
Perguntas no passado precisam de did (exceto com was/were).

grammar.title: Past continuous + simple past
grammar.explanation_pt:
O **past continuous** descreve uma ação **em andamento** em um momento do passado. É o "estava fazendo".

**Estrutura:** was / were + verbo-ing
- I **was cooking** at 8 p.m. (às 20h eu estava cozinhando)

O uso mais comum é com o **simple past**, para mostrar uma ação longa (**background**) **interrompida** por uma ação curta:

- I **was cooking** (ação longa) **when** the phone **rang** (ação curta).
- **While** I **was walking** to work, I **saw** an accident.

**When** + simple past (ação curta) · **While** + past continuous (ação longa).

Duas ações longas ao mesmo tempo: "**While** I **was working**, my kids **were playing**."

examples.en: I was taking a shower when the doorbell rang.
examples.pt: Eu estava tomando banho quando a campainha tocou.

examples.en: While she was texting, she walked into a pole!
examples.pt: Enquanto mandava mensagem, ela bateu num poste!

examples.en: What were you doing when the earthquake happened?
examples.pt: O que você estava fazendo quando o terremoto aconteceu?

grammar.tip_pt: Stative verbs também não usam -ing no passado: "I **knew** the answer" (e não "I was knowing").

common_mistakes.wrong: I cooked when the phone was ringing.
common_mistakes.right: I was cooking when the phone rang.
common_mistakes.why_pt: A ação longa fica no past continuous; a curta, no simple past.

common_mistakes.wrong: While I walked to work, I was seeing an accident.
common_mistakes.right: While I was walking to work, I saw an accident.
common_mistakes.why_pt: While + ação longa (past continuous); a interrupção no simple past.

pronunciation.tip_pt: Em "I was cooking", o **was** é rápido e fraco ("ái uâz kúkin"). A força vai no verbo principal: "I was **COOK**ing when the phone **RANG**."

grammar.title: Conectores de narrativa
grammar.explanation_pt:
Uma boa história em inglês tem **estrutura** e **conectores**:

**1. Começo (cenário)** — past continuous + was/were:
"It **was** a rainy Friday. I **was driving** home..."
**2. Problema** — simple past + **suddenly**:
"**Suddenly**, the car **stopped**."
**3. Sequência** — **then, after that, so, because, but**:
"I **called** my brother, **but** he didn't answer, **so** I **walked**."
**4. Final** — **luckily / unfortunately, in the end, finally**:
"**In the end**, a nice guy **helped** me."

**So x because:** so mostra a **consequência** (então); because mostra a **causa** (porque).
- It was late, **so** I took a taxi. / I took a taxi **because** it was late.

**Reagir** também faz parte: Really? / No way! / Oh no! / Then what? / What happened next?

rows: One day... / It all started when... / At first...
Luckily... / Unfortunately... / In the end... / Finally...

examples.en: It all started when I was waiting for my flight in Lima.
examples.pt: Tudo começou quando eu esperava meu voo em Lima.

examples.en: The flight was cancelled, so I stayed one more night.
examples.pt: O voo foi cancelado, então fiquei mais uma noite.

examples.en: Unfortunately, my bag didn't arrive. Luckily, I had my passport.
examples.pt: Infelizmente, minha mala não chegou. Por sorte, eu estava com meu passaporte.

grammar.tip_pt: **In the end** = no final (da história). **At the end** (of) = no fim de algo: at the end of the movie, at the end of the street.

common_mistakes.wrong: It was late, because I took a taxi.
common_mistakes.right: It was late, so I took a taxi.

common_mistakes.wrong: In the final, everything was OK.
common_mistakes.right: In the end, everything was OK.

common_mistakes.why_pt: Varie os conectores para a história ficar natural.

pronunciation.focus: Pausas e ênfase ao contar histórias
pronunciation.tip_pt: Bons contadores de histórias fazem **pausas** antes do momento importante e **enfatizam** as palavras-chave: "And then... (pausa) SUDDENLY... the lights went OUT." Grave-se contando e ouça!
practice: And then... suddenly... the lights went out!
Luckily, in the end, everything was fine.

dialogue.title: The airport story
dialogue.context_pt: Num bar, um amigo conta uma história de viagem e o outro reage.

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.en: You won't believe what happened on my trip to Chile!
lines.pt: Você não vai acreditar no que aconteceu na minha viagem ao Chile!

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.en: What happened?
lines.pt: O que aconteceu?

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.en: Well, it all started at the airport. I was waiting for my flight and I fell asleep.
lines.pt: Bom, tudo começou no aeroporto. Eu estava esperando meu voo e peguei no sono.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.en: No way! Did you miss the flight?
lines.pt: Não acredito! Você perdeu o voo?

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.en: Almost! Suddenly, I heard my name: "Last call for passenger Rafael Lima!" So I ran to the gate.
lines.pt: Quase! De repente, ouvi meu nome: "Última chamada para o passageiro Rafael Lima!" Então corri para o portão.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.en: And then?
lines.pt: E aí?

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.en: Luckily, they waited for me. But everybody on the plane was looking at me. In the end, the woman next to me became a good friend!
lines.pt: Por sorte, eles me esperaram. Mas todo mundo no avião estava olhando para mim. No final, a mulher ao meu lado virou uma boa amiga!

listening.title: Story time podcast
listening.context_pt: Uma ouvinte conta uma história em um podcast.

lines.speaker: Paula
lines.en: One night last winter, I was walking home from work. It was cold and dark. At first, everything was normal. Then I realized someone was following me. I walked faster, and the person walked faster too! I was really scared, so I went into a pharmacy. Suddenly, the person came in and said, "Excuse me! You dropped this!" It was my wallet. In the end, he wasn't a criminal — he was a very nice guy. I felt so silly!

questions.q: Why did she go into a pharmacy?
Why was the man following her?
questions.answer: Because she dropped her wallet and he wanted to give it back.

reading.title: A short story: The last bus
reading.text: It was a rainy night in London, and Ana was waiting for the last bus. She was tired after a long day at the restaurant. At first, the street was empty. Then an old man arrived. He was carrying a big box. "Is this the bus to Camden?" he asked. "Yes," said Ana. Suddenly, the box moved! The man smiled and opened it: there was a small, wet puppy inside. "I found him in the rain," he said, "but I can't keep him. My apartment doesn't allow dogs." Ana looked at the puppy, and the puppy looked at Ana. In the end, two passengers got off the bus that night: Ana and her new dog, Lucky.

questions.answer: Because she worked a long day at the restaurant.

questions.q: Why couldn't the man keep the puppy?
questions.answer: Because his apartment doesn't allow dogs.
Ana took the puppy home and named him Lucky.

exercises.title: Story connectors
exercises.instruction: Complete with: One day · Suddenly · so · Luckily · In the end.

items.prompt: ___, I was hiking in the mountains.

I met Neymar at the airport!

So I opened the door and...

items.answer: It all started when I was at the airport.
In the end, everything was fine.

items.prompt: It was cold, because I wore a jacket.
items.answer: It was cold, so I wore a jacket.

items.prompt: In the final, we were friends.
items.answer: In the end, we were friends.

exercises.title: Put the story in order
exercises.instruction: Put the sentences in the correct order (write the letters).
exercises.instruction_pt: Coloque as frases na ordem certa (escreva as letras).

items.prompt: a) Suddenly, I heard a noise in the kitchen. / b) In the end, it was my cat eating the cake! / c) One night, I was watching a movie alone. / d) I was scared, so I took my phone and walked slowly to the kitchen.

speaking.instruction: Tell a 1–2 minute story (true or invented). Use at least 5 connectors. Your partner reacts and asks questions.
speaking.instruction_pt: Conte uma história de 1–2 minutos (verdadeira ou inventada). Use pelo menos 5 conectores. O colega reage e faz perguntas.
questions: Tell me about a crazy trip.
Tell me about a time you were really scared.
Tell me about a lucky moment in your life.
What's a funny family story?
Tell me about a time something went wrong.

writing.task: Write a short story (100–120 words) that starts with "It was a dark and stormy night..." or a true story from your life. Use past simple, past continuous and connectors.
writing.task_pt: Escreva uma história curta (100–120 palavras) começando com "It was a dark and stormy night..." ou uma história real da sua vida. Use past simple, past continuous e conectores.
writing.model: It was a dark and stormy night. I was home alone, and I was reading a book in bed. Suddenly, the lights went out. At first, I wasn't worried, so I looked for a candle. Then I heard footsteps in the living room! I was terrified, but I took my umbrella — my only weapon — and walked slowly to the door. I opened it and screamed. Luckily, it was only my brother. He forgot his keys, so he came in through the window. In the end, we laughed for hours and ate ice cream in the dark.

culture_note.title: Storytelling e stand-up
culture_note.text_pt: A cultura de língua inglesa valoriza muito contar histórias: o stand-up comedy, os podcasts como **The Moth** e os TED Talks são basicamente histórias pessoais bem contadas. Assistir a esses formatos é ótimo treino de listening no passado.

summary_pt: Reaja: Really? No way! What happened next?

review.intro_pt: Revise o passado completo: was/were, simple past, past continuous e narrativas.

It was late, ___ we went home.
There ___ a lot of cars on the road.

items.answer: Where did you go on vacation?

items.answer: I was driving when I saw the accident.
There were a lot of people at the concert.
While I was cooking, I burned my finger.

review.speaking_pt: Grave um áudio de 2 minutos contando uma história real da sua vida (viagem, acidente engraçado, um encontro importante). Use todos os tempos do passado deste módulo.
speaking_questions: Where were you and what were you doing?
review.project_pt: **Story night:** organize uma "noite de histórias" com a turma (ou grave um mini-podcast): cada pessoa conta uma história de 1 a 2 minutos e os outros reagem e fazem perguntas. Bônus: vote na melhor história!
